To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the short and long isoforms of the gamma 1 subunit of the gamma 3 subunit of the receptor are expressed differentially in different brain regions and neurons, with the long form predominating in the striate cortex and the cerebellar Purkinge cell layer and the short form predominating in neurons of the olfactory and pyriform cortex as well as the dentate gyrux and hippocampus.

the GABAA receptors are assembled from several subunits that are differentially expressed in different brain regions and cell types and that this heterogeneity may be important in the modulation of GABAergic function.

the GABAA receptors are heteromultimers of several protein subunits and that these subunits are differentially expressed in different neurons and brain regions, which may result in differential ethanol and benzodiazepine sensitivity of different neurons and brain areas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the differential expression and function of the gamma 1, gamma 2L and gamma 2S subunits of the gamma subfamily in GABAA receptors.
the differential distribution of GABAA receptor gamma 2 subunits.
the differential expression of the gamma 1, gamma 2S, gamma 2L, gamma 3, delta, alpha 1-6, beta 1-3, and rho 1 subunits of the rat GABAA receptor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gamma 2S subunits are expressed in the majority of neurons, whereas gamma 2L expression is restricted to a subset of neurons.

the gamma 2L-containing GABAA receptors are more abundant in the brain regions where ethanol exerts anxiolytic and motor-activating effects and that gamma 2S-containing receptors are more abundant where ethanol exerts sedative and motor-depressing effects.
gamma 2S subunits are preferentially expressed in the hippocampus, the olfactory bulb and pyriform cortex whereas gamma 2L is preferentially expressed in neocortical areas and the cerebellum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a regional and cellular heterogeneity of the GAB AA receptors/benzodiezepine receptors in the rat brain.

the gamma 2L and gamma 2S subunits have a differential and selective expression in the brain and that this expression pattern is reflected in the differential expression of the gamma 1S and gamma 1L subunits of GABAA receptors in the brain.

the gamma 2L and gamma 2S subunits of the rat GABAA/bz receptors are differentially expressed in the brain, with gamma 2L being enriched in cerebellum, superior and inferior colliculi, and deep nuclei of cerebellum, and gamma 2s being enriched in olfactory bulb, hippocampus, and neocortex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a differential expression of gamma 1S and gamma 1L in the brain.
the GABAA receptors in neurons of the cerebellum and inferior colliculus are enriched in gamma2L subunits.
gamma 2S is the predominant form of the gamma 1-2-3-4 receptor complex in most brain regions and that gamma 2L is expressed in a subset of neurons that are enriched in GABAergic synapses.
